name: Field Doctor-Style Italian Beef Meatballs (Low FODMAP)
ingredients:
1365 g Extra Lean Beef
2 x 400 g tins Plum Tomato
415 g Penne Pasta (GLUTEN FREE) [brown rice flour]
2 3/4 medium Carrots
70 g Spinach
1/4 Green Peppers
1 1/4 tbsp Tomato Puree [tomato]
6.3 g Fennel
1 1/2 tsp Parmigiano (MILK) [MILK Salt, Microbial Enzymes]
1.9 g Red Quinoa
2/3 tsp Quinoa Flour
1 1/2 tsp Mixed Herbs
1 tsp Parsley Flat
1.5 g Chives
2/3 tsp Sweet Noble Paprika
1.5 g Sundried Tomatoes [Sundried tomatoes, Salt]
1/2 tsp Tapioca Starch
1.5 g Quinoa Flake
2/3 tsp Flax Seeds
1/3 tsp Beef Stock [Beef Extract, Water, Salt]
1/4 tsp Tamari [water, SOYA beans, sea salt]
1/3 tsp Red Wine Vinegar
1/3 tsp Sea Salt
1/4 tsp Celery Salt (CELERY)
2/3 tsp Black Pepper
2/3 tsp Oregano
3/4 tsp Fennel Ground
directions:
1. Meatballs: Mix extra-lean beef with quinoa flour, quinoa flakes, flax seeds, grated hard cheese, herb mix, paprika, oregano, ground fennel, celery salt, black pepper and a splash of tamari. Form into walnut-sized meatballs.

2. Brown: Heat extra virgin olive oil in a wide pan and brown the meatballs on all sides. Set aside.

3. Sauce: In the same pan, soften diced carrot, green pepper and fennel with chives. Stir in chopped tomato, tomato puree, sundried tomatoes, beef stock, red wine vinegar and oregano. Simmer 10–15 minutes until slightly thickened; loosen with water if needed. Stir a little tapioca starch slurry in if you want it thicker.

4. Pasta: Boil gluten-free brown-rice penne in salted water until just al dente. Drain, keeping a splash of cooking water.

5. Finish: Return meatballs to the sauce with spinach until wilted. Toss through the penne (and a little red quinoa if you cooked it alongside). Adjust seasoning. Serve with parsley and more hard cheese.
 
Cool, portion into 8, refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze; reheat until piping hot.

Home recreation inspired by Field Doctor Italian Beef Meatballs (Low FODMAP) (~382 g ready meal). Scaled to 8 portions. Not an official Field Doctor recipe. https://www.fielddoctor.co.uk/products/italian-beef-meatballs-low-fodmap
notes:
REVERSE-ENGINEERED from Field Doctor published ingredients for personal home cooking only. Official meal is Monash Low FODMAP certified at single-serve size.

Scaling notes
Scaled for 8 portions from Field Doctor single serve (~382 g x 8 = 3056 g).
Unlabelled amounts inferred from UK descending-weight ingredient order (each item <= the one above and >= the one below; leftover mass shared on that basis, not equally).
Spoon measures use ingredient density (g per tsp) then round to kitchen fractions.
Amounts above 50 g are rounded to the nearest 5 g for cooking convenience.
Sweet peppers ~140 g each; carrots ~80 g; sweet potatoes ~130 g; courgettes ~175 g; aubergines ~250 g; swedes ~800 g; plum tomatoes = 400 g tins; lemon ~45 ml / lime ~30 ml juice.
Duplicate label ingredients merged (higher amount kept).
Liquid for home cooking: cook rice, quinoa, pasta, noodles and potatoes in water as you normally would (salt the water; drain where appropriate). For sauces, braises and stir-fry glazes, add water or stock gradually until the consistency is right — do not try to measure the ready-meal's residual water.
Low FODMAP: no onion or garlic bulbs — use chives / green tops only. Inspired recreation from Field Doctor ingredients, not an official recipe.
Chives listed in grams to match fresh packs (e.g. Waitrose Cooks' Ingredients Chives, 20 g).
Ready-meal residual water was ~125 g (inferred ~4.09% from list order) and is not listed as an ingredient.
Oil for home cooking: where Extra Virgin Olive Oil was only a cooking fat on the label, it is omitted from ingredients — fry, soften, sear or roast in extra virgin olive oil as needed. It is kept as an ingredient on richer/oil-forward dishes (e.g. pesto-style sauces or high oil content).
Ready-meal residual Extra Virgin Olive Oil was ~11 g (inferred ~0.37% from list order) and is treated as cooking fat (fry in extra virgin olive oil) rather than a measured ingredient.
